title: Brass bands and funeral hymns
summary: Names other brass bands and explains that non-readers played funerals by ear; he recalls the first hymns bands played coming back.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, did they have any other brass bands? Oh, yeah. Who were some of the other ones?
Allen. Old Man Allen. Tulane, Amos Riley. Mm-hmm.
Did they have any strictly head brass bands?

Well, just jazz like, you know. Yeah. Most of them bands tried to read them dodges. Yeah. Most of them bands, old Man Allen. All them that couldn't, he'd always get the men that could read, you see. Yeah. That's one thing.
They always wanted to play them dodges. Oh, yeah.

Yeah. And now some guys like Foster, you know, they would get a brass band. Maybe he might know some people uptown got a club or borrow them or something, they're picking up some money, you know, to get a band, you know, like the Caledonia do, you know, see. Well they would pick up anybody and go ahead and play the funeral, you know, play them funeral marches by head, you know, lead me savior, narrow my God to thee, you know, and that was it. That was all. You see they could play. But when it comes down to real, dodges, I don't know. What would they play coming back in those bands? Well they played Denny Rambo, you know, see, and that was before Saints, you know, see, and other different things. But Sing On, that was the first hymn I heard them play Sing On. That was the first hymn, well after the little bands got that, but we never did play them for dances. No, we played for dances. Saints was the only first hymn that I heard the bands play. Yeah.
